$doc: Vyomi capability registry — Azure Key vaults. See aws/s3.json for the contract.

azure.keyvaults.vault.crud.title: Vaults (create, get, list, delete) over ARM

azure.keyvaults.access_configuration.title: Access configuration (RBAC vs vault access policy, resource access flags)
limitations: enableRbacAuthorization and the resource-access flags are stored and returned exactly as written, but Vyomi does not enforce them. Real Key Vault data-plane calls are routed by the vault's own hostname ({vault}.vault.azure.net); Vyomi's Key Vault Keys/Secrets/Certificates REST data planes sit behind one shared, vault-agnostic relay (same simplification the AWS lens makes for KMS/Secrets Manager key policies), so a keys/secrets call carries no wire signal identifying which vault's access model should apply — enforcing against a guessed vault would deny or allow calls incorrectly rather than modelling the real control.

azure.keyvaults.access_policies.title: Vault access policies (properties.accessPolicies)
limitations: Access policy entries round-trip through ARM exactly as written, but Vyomi never evaluates them — every data-plane key/secret call succeeds regardless of the configured permissions. Same root cause as azure.keyvaults.access_configuration: the data-plane relay is shared across every vault (no per-vault hostname), so a call has no wire signal saying which vault's access-policy list to check.

azure.keyvaults.networking.title: Networking (public network access / firewall default action)
limitations: publicNetworkAccess and networkAcls round-trip through ARM, but the Key Vault Keys/Secrets REST data planes never enforce them — a call from a 'denied' network still succeeds. Same root cause as azure.keyvaults.access_configuration: the data-plane relay has no per-vault hostname, so it cannot tell which vault's firewall config a given call should be checked against.

azure.keyvaults.keys.crud.title: Keys (create, get, list, delete) over the Key Vault Keys REST API

azure.keyvaults.keys.crypto.title: Key encrypt/decrypt/wrap/unwrap/sign/verify
limitations: The RSA public numbers (n/e) advertised on a key are cosmetic (deterministically derived from the private material); the actual cipher behind encrypt/decrypt/wrap/unwrap is a symmetric authenticated envelope, and sign/verify is HMAC-based rather than native RSA/ECDSA. Round-trips (encrypt→decrypt, sign→verify, tamper/cross-key rejection) are real.

azure.keyvaults.secrets.crud.title: Secrets (set, get, list, list versions, delete) over the Key Vault Secrets REST API

azure.keyvaults.certificates.title: Certificates (generate self-signed, import, get, list, delete) over the Key Vault Certificates REST API
limitations: Generated (self-signed) certificate creation completes synchronously, and GET .../pending always reports the operation already 'completed' — there is no real multi-step issuance to poll. The `cer`/`x5t` on a GENERATED certificate are deterministic cosmetic bytes, not real X.509 DER.

Importing a PEM certificate is real: the `-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----` block is decoded and its actual DER becomes `cer`, with `x5t` the real SHA-1 thumbprint of that DER. A password-protected PFX (PKCS#12) `value` is accepted but not parsed — this substrate has no ASN.1/PKCS#12 library, so it falls back to the same cosmetic bytes as a generated certificate. Either way the expiration attribute is derived from the request policy's validity_in_months, not read from the certificate's own ASN.1 validity period.
CA-issued certificates (a real external certificate authority) are not simulated on any substrate.

azure.keyvaults.locks.title: Resource locks (Microsoft.Authorization/locks), scoped to this vault
limitations: Locks are only simulated at the resource scope (this vault); subscription- and resource-group-scoped lock lists are an honest 'Not simulated' gap, same as the real Subscription/Resource group scope-switch buttons.

azure.keyvaults.activity_log.title: Activity log
limitations: Only console/SDK-triggered mutations made since the simulation booted are recorded (no historical backfill); severity/category filtering and the 7/30/90-day timespan picker are not modelled, and `caller` is a fixed placeholder identity rather than the real signed-in principal.
